content.comment_body: I'm experiencing issues setting up basic communication with a [product_name] module without a display. Previously, I used units with displays where setting a known IP address was straightforward. Without the display, I'm unsure how to connect it to my PC. Based on forum suggestions, I tried the default IP address (192.168.0.1), but that hasn't worked. Can anyone provide basic guidance on what steps I should try?
Could you share the current IP address of your PC?

Both your PC and the [product_name] should be in the same IP address range. For example, the format should be XXX.YYY.ZZZ.nnn, where XXX.YYY.ZZZ matches for both devices and only nnn differs. Sample IPs could be: PC = 192.168.178.12, [product_name] = 192.168.178.13. Ensure the subnet mask is the same too, such as 255.255.255.0. To set a new IP address on the [product_name], create a program, specify the desired IP and subnet mask in its properties, then transfer it to the device. During the transfer, select the correct target IP and complete the process. You'll be prompted to overwrite the IP address; confirm to finalize the change.

Thanks for your reply, [user_name]. My main problem is that I can't establish any basic communication needed to start a download. Following your advice, I connected my PC and [product_name] directly via Ethernet, manually entered IP and subnet mask in my PC settings (using TCP/IP options on Windows 7), and set the same in the [product_name] program details. I even tried transferring the corresponding program with the assigned IP to an SD card and booted the device with it. Despite several attempts, [product_name] configuration software doesn't detect the device. Any further suggestions?

Using the SD card method isn't ideal. If you want to update the IP address of the [product_name], starting the device with the SD card will overwrite it with the address from the card's program. Start your PC and use "ipconfig" to provide: • PC’s IP address • PC’s subnet mask. Do you have a direct cable connection between PC and [product_name], or are you going through a router? If it's through a router, what are the router’s IP address and subnet mask?

Hi, What is the name of the Ethernet interface you're using? If the name contains special characters, it might not work properly, as Windows isn't fully compatible with those for Ethernet driver naming (see example image). To connect: 1. Directly connect your PC to the [product_name] with a cable and check the Ethernet connection properties. 2. Open TCP/IPv4 settings. 3. Select an IP address within the same subnet as the [product_name] (default IP: 192.168.0.1). 4. Complete the IP settings and start [product_name] configuration software V8. 5. Switch to network project mode and press "Go Online". After a few seconds, the [product_name] and its IP should appear in the network view. Hope that helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties establishing basic network communication between their PC and a [product_name] module lacking a display, primarily due to IP address configuration and recognition issues with the configuration software. The inability to set or confirm IP addresses directly on the device leads to confusion and connectivity failures. Despite attempts using direct Ethernet connections, manual IP address setup, and software detection, users report that the [product_name] configuration software does not locate the device, so setup remains incomplete.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate being able to easily configure, retrieve, and verify the device's IP address, even without a hardware display, and expect the configuration software to reliably recognize a connected device for straightforward network setup.
